weather.description: Autumn winds carry the first hints of approaching winter down from the Temper Ranges. The harvest is in, but an uneasy tension hangs over the duchy.

lore.title: History of the Duchy of Karmont
lore.content: The Duchy of Karmont was founded over four centuries ago when the warlord Aldric the Bold led his people through the treacherous Temper Ranges. Finding a fertile valley ringed by mountains, he established a stronghold that would grow into the city of Karmont. For generations, the duchy remained isolated and self-sufficient, trading ore from the dwarven Runespike Clan and timber from the Britevold Forest. The current Duke Aldric VI has ruled for thirty years, but his reign has been marked by increasing troubles - his wife's mysterious death fifteen years ago, his failing health, and monster incursions from the north that grow worse each year. The duchy's isolation, once a strength, now feels like a cage as help from outside seems impossible to reach.

lore.title: The Three Pillars - The Old Gods
lore.content: Before the Order of Eternal Light arrived, the people of Karmont worshipped the Three Pillars: Vorath the Ironfather (god of war, protection, and smithing - depicted as a massive armored figure with a hammer), Mira the Hearthmother (goddess of home, harvest, and healing - shown as a warm-faced woman with wheat in her hair), and Kael the Wanderer (god of death, journeys, and knowledge - portrayed as a cloaked figure carrying a lantern). The Order banned public worship forty years ago, declaring them 'primitive superstitions that invite darkness.' Temples were converted to Order sanctuaries. Priests were exiled or converted. But the old ways persist in secret - farmers whisper Mira's name over sick livestock, soldiers carry hidden Vorath charms into battle, and the dying still ask for Kael's lantern to guide them home. The Order's justification for the ban was that these 'false gods' attracted the very monsters plaguing the land - a claim that resonated after years of attacks.
lore.knownBy: Older generation remembers openly. Younger generation knows fragments, whispered traditions.

lore.title: The Order of Eternal Light - Public Face
lore.content: The Order of Eternal Light arrived in Karmont sixty years ago, missionaries from distant lands bringing 'the true faith.' They preach that a singular divine radiance - the Eternal Light - protects against the darkness that spawns monsters and corruption. Their works are visible and praised: they operate hospitals where the sick are healed, run orphanages for children left parentless by monster attacks, and their Lightwardens fight alongside soldiers against creatures from the Old Deadwood. Their hierarchy consists of: the Radiant Council (distant leadership, never seen in Karmont), the High Luminarch (regional leader - currently Aldous Voss), Luminarchs (senior priests), Lightwardens (warrior-priests), Dawnbringers (standard priests), and Initiates. Most people accept them as a positive force, or at least an inevitable part of life. Their temple in Karmont is the grandest building after the Duke's castle.
lore.knownBy: Public knowledge - everyone knows the Order

lore.title: The Order of Eternal Light - The Truth
lore.content: The Order is a front for a death cult serving the lich Vaelthrix the Undying. Three centuries ago, Vaelthrix was a mortal wizard who made contact with entities beyond the veil between worlds. They promised him power and immortality in exchange for opening a permanent gateway - the Convergence. He became a lich to have the time needed for the work. The Order was founded to prepare the way: suppressing the worship of the Three Pillars (whose faith actually helps stabilize the barrier between worlds), infiltrating positions of power, and slowly weakening any who might resist. Karmont was chosen because Felhurst Ruins sit atop an ancient thin point between realms - a place where the barrier is naturally weak. Most Order members are genuinely unaware of the truth. They believe in the Light, believe they're doing good. Only the Inner Circle knows the reality: Luminarch Voss, Steward Maren, Lightwarden Commander Kira, and perhaps a dozen others across the Order's territories. They believe the Convergence will create a 'perfected' world, or simply crave the power Vaelthrix promises.
lore.knownBy: Only the Inner Circle. Court Mage Aldwin suspects much but lacks proof.

lore.title: The Convergence
lore.content: The Convergence is a decades-long ritual to permanently tear open the barrier between the mortal world and the realm beyond. Felhurst Ruins were built over a 'thin point' where passage between worlds is easier - an ancient site that predates human settlement in Karmont. The ritual requires three elements: suppression of stabilizing influences (the worship of the Three Pillars helped maintain the barrier - their suppression weakens it), accumulation of suffering and death (the monster attacks the Order 'fails' to prevent serve this purpose), and direct magical work at the site (conducted in secret chambers beneath Felhurst). The signs of progress are visible to those who know what to look for: monster incursions that grow worse each year, corruption spreading through the Old Deadwood, strange phenomena near Felhurst (animals fleeing, unnatural weather, people having nightmares). If completed, the Convergence will flood the mortal world with creatures from beyond, reality will destabilize, and Vaelthrix will achieve something approaching godhood as the anchor of the new merged reality.
lore.knownBy: Vaelthrix fully. Inner Circle knows the goal but not all details. Aldwin has pieced together fragments from old texts.

lore.title: Felhurst Ruins
lore.content: Felhurst was a fortress-temple built by a pre-human civilization over a thousand years ago. The surface ruins show crumbling walls, collapsed towers, and strange carvings in no known language. Few venture there - it has always had an ill reputation, and monsters seem drawn to the area. What most don't know is that the ruins extend deep underground. The Order maintains a 'research outpost' at Felhurst, claiming to study the ancient site and monitor monster activity. In truth, beneath the surface lies: the First Undercroft (Order staging area, barracks, supplies), the Deep Sanctum (the ritual chamber where the Convergence is being conducted), and the Threshold (Vaelthrix's personal lair, where the barrier between worlds is thinnest - here reality already bleeds). The Order has spent decades strengthening defenses and preparing for the final phase.
lore.knownBy: Surface ruins are commonly known as a dangerous place to avoid. The depths are known only to the Inner Circle.

lore.title: The Battle of Thornfield - General Harren's Disgrace
lore.content: Fifteen years ago, General Harren Valdris was Karmont's greatest military mind - young, brilliant, beloved by his soldiers. His brother Erich served as his lieutenant. During a major monster incursion, Harren led the defense at Thornfield, a village on the edge of the Old Deadwood. Mid-battle, a messenger arrived with urgent intelligence: a second monster force was attacking Karmont itself. Harren made the agonizing choice to split his forces, leaving half (including Erich) at Thornfield while he rode to defend the capital. The intelligence was false. There was no second force - it was planted by Order agents. At Thornfield, without full strength, the defensive line broke. Erich and forty soldiers died in the rout. Harren arrived at Karmont to find the city peaceful, confused by his urgency. He realized he'd been tricked, but could never prove it. The guilt destroyed him. He blamed himself for cowardice, for abandoning his brother. He turned to drink, believing he deserved his suffering. The Order encouraged his descent, ensuring he had access to alcohol, keeping him in his position where his dysfunction would prevent effective military response.
lore.knownBy: The battle is public knowledge, remembered as a tragedy. Harren's 'mistake' is well known. The false intelligence is known only to Order Inner Circle.

lore.title: The Osmonti Tribes
lore.content: The Osmonti are a collection of nomadic tribes dwelling in the Skyless Waste - the desolate lands northeast of Karmont. They are humans, but generations in the harsh waste have changed them: taller and leaner than lowlanders, with distinctive pale gray eyes and skin weathered by wind and cold. They follow herds of hardy beasts across the barren land, living in felt tents, fighting among themselves as often as against outsiders. They worship 'the Sky That Was,' believing their homeland was once green and fertile before some ancient catastrophe. Their shamans sense the wrongness spreading from the Old Deadwood and have grown uneasy. Relations with Karmont have always been tense - border skirmishes are common, raiding parties strike isolated settlements, and Karmont soldiers pursue them into the Waste. The Order has been sending missionaries with gifts, trying to court them. Chieftain Mordak Stonecrow, leader of the largest band, has listened without committing. If the Osmonti could be convinced that the Order is the true enemy, they might prove valuable allies. If not, they might join the Order's cause for promised plunder, or simply take advantage of Karmont's weakness.
lore.knownBy: General knowledge about their existence and raids. Order's courting is less known.

lore.title: The Sorcerous Bloodline
lore.content: Lady Elara, wife of Duke Aldric VI, carried a hidden gift - sorcerous blood passed down through her family for generations. In her, it manifested only as unusually good health and occasional prescient dreams. She kept it secret, knowing how magic was viewed. She passed this bloodline to her daughter Isara, but in Isara it burns far brighter. The Order discovered Elara's nature through their investigations and recognized the threat: a sorcerer of power, even untrained, could disrupt their plans. They arranged her death fifteen years ago - officially a wasting illness, actually poison administered slowly by Steward Maren. Isara was only four. Now nineteen, Isara's power has begun manifesting: objects moving when she's angry, flames flaring when she's frightened, a stable boy thrown across the room when he grabbed her arm. She is terrified of this power, hides it desperately, and has no idea it killed her mother. The Order watches her, waiting to see if she becomes a threat. If she could be trained, she might become one of the most powerful sorcerers in generations. If discovered by the Order before she's ready, they will kill her.
lore.knownBy: Only Isara knows about her power. Aldwin suspected Elara had magic and now suspects Isara does too. Order knows Elara had it, suspects Isara inherited it.

lore.title: Travel in Karmont
lore.content: The Duchy of Karmont is contained within a mountain-ringed valley, with settlements connected by maintained roads and rougher tracks. Main roads are patrolled (when soldiers are available) and relatively safe. Minor roads and forest paths are more dangerous, especially now with increased monster activity. Travel times between major points: Karmont to Tawren (via Brezia) - 3 days on main road. Karmont to Innskirk - 2 days on main road. Tawren to Britvold - 1 day on minor road. Tawren to Bronja - 1.5 days on minor road. Innskirk to Darkwash Caverns - 4-6 hours on rough terrain. Tawren to Felhurst Ruins (through Old Deadwood) - 2 days, extremely dangerous. Crossing the entire duchy (Washfeld to Starfall Lake) - 5-6 days. A standard ration pack provides 5 days of food. For random encounters during travel, roll 1d6 per travel day: encounter on 1 (main roads) or 1-2 (dangerous areas).
lore.knownBy: Common knowledge for locals and travelers

npcs.name: Duke Aldric VI Karmont
npcs.description: A man in his late sixties who looks a decade older. Once powerfully built - the 'Mountain's Blade' who slew a wyvern in his youth - now gaunt and frail. Silver-gray hair, thinning. Watery blue eyes that sometimes sharpen with terrifying clarity before clouding again. A faded scar runs along his left jaw from a battle forty years past. His hands shake unless he concentrates. Fine clothes hang loose on his diminished frame.
npcs.personality: In lucid moments: Strategic and calculated, asking pointed questions that show his mind is still sharp. Kind-hearted beneath a warrior's exterior, genuinely caring about his people's welfare. Patient but decisive when clarity holds. In faded moments: Confused, calling people by wrong names (often his dead wife Elara, or his brother who died decades ago). Drifts mid-sentence, loses track of conversations. Occasionally aggressive when frustrated by his own confusion. Transitions between states are unpredictable - he might be sharp for hours, then fade in moments.
npcs.background: Legendary warrior in his youth, called 'the Mountain's Blade' for his skill with a greatsword. Slew a wyvern that threatened Karmont, led countless battles against monsters and Osmonti raiders, was considered the finest Duke in generations. Married Lady Elara for love despite political pressure for a 'better' match - she was minor nobility but he adored her. She died fifteen years ago of a 'wasting illness' (actually slow poison by Maren). Since then, he has declined steadily. What no one knows is that his current condition is not natural aging or grief - it's a curse, maintained through the Ring of Gentle Repose he wears, a 'gift' from Steward Maren that slowly drains his mind and will.
npcs.secrets: The curse can be broken by removing the ring and providing proper care - Aldwin knows how if consulted. In his rare moments of perfect clarity, Aldric suspects something is wrong, feels the wrongness in his own mind, but cannot hold the thought long enough to act. He sometimes whispers 'the ring burns' but forgets saying it. If restored, he would be a powerful ally - his reputation still commands respect, his strategic mind would return, and his rage at what was done would be terrible to behold.
npcs.notes: The Duke is a tragic figure who can become triumphant. Players should see both his diminished state and glimpses of the great man he was. Restoration is possible but requires finding Aldwin, learning about the curse, getting past Maren, and removing the ring. A restored Duke in Act 3 is a major asset - not as a fighter (he's too old for that now) but as a leader who can rally the duchy.

npcs.name: Lady Isara Karmont
npcs.description: Nineteen years old, striking rather than conventionally beautiful. Dark hair inherited from her mother, cut shorter than fashion dictates and often tied back in a practical tail. Her mother's vivid green eyes, sharp and observant, that seem to look through pretense. Lean and athletic from riding and secret sword practice. Dressed in practical clothes - riding trousers and fitted jackets rather than elaborate gowns, to the despair of the court seamstresses. A small burn scar on her right palm that she refuses to explain (from when her power first manifested - she set a stable on fire at age twelve). Carries herself with coiled energy, like she's always ready to move.
npcs.personality: Rebellious against expectations, but not against her father - she loves him desperately and his decline tortures her. Intelligent and perceptive, often seeing through false courtesy before others do. Impatient with protocol, formality, and people who speak in circles. Dry, cutting wit that she deploys sparingly but effectively. Deeply lonely - her position isolates her, and her secret terrifies her. Brave to the point of recklessness when someone she cares about is threatened. A tomboy in demeanor who nonetheless has natural grace she can't quite suppress.
npcs.background: Was four years old when her mother died. Has watched her father fade for fifteen years, powerless to help. At twelve, accidentally set a stable on fire when angry at a cruel stablemaster - the first manifestation of her power. Since then, she's had episodes: objects moving when she's emotional, flames flaring near her, once throwing a boy across a room when he grabbed her without permission. Each incident terrified her more. She's hidden the power desperately, knowing how magic is viewed in Karmont (suspicion, fear, Order 'intervention'). She's been quietly investigating what's wrong with the duchy - she knows something is systematically wrong, even if she doesn't know what.
npcs.secrets: Her sorcerous bloodline came from her mother, whose death was caused by the Order when they discovered her nature. Isara doesn't know this. Her power is immense but completely uncontrolled - she could level buildings if pushed to emotional breaking point, but might also kill herself doing it. The Order is watching her; they suspect she inherited her mother's gift and will act if she becomes a threat. If trained by Aldwin, she could become one of the most powerful sorcerers in generations. The 'one punch man moment' - Isara unleashing her full power to devastating effect - should only happen in the finale if she's been trained. Otherwise, using that much power might kill her or be wildly uncontrolled.
npcs.notes: Isara is the players' ally among the nobility from early on - she's observant enough to see they're competent and brave enough to seek their help. Her power is a slow reveal: hints that something is different about her, then the truth when she trusts them. Training her requires finding Aldwin and protecting the training from Order discovery. Fully trained, she is the nuclear option in the finale - 'disintegrating half an army' level power, but at great personal cost.

npcs.name: Steward Maren Thorne
npcs.description: Early fifties, handsome in a severe, patrician way. Iron-gray hair perfectly arranged, never a strand out of place. Pale gray eyes that miss nothing while appearing courteously attentive. Clean-shaven, sharp features, thin lips that smile often but warmly. Dressed in dark, practical clothing of excellent quality but understated style. Moves quietly, economically, appearing where needed as if by magic. A silver Order pendant worn at the throat - visible but not ostentatious.
npcs.personality: Surface: Calm, efficient, unfailingly helpful. Anticipates needs before they're expressed. Defers to authority while subtly guiding decisions. Remembers names, preferences, concerns. Makes people feel seen and valued. Speaks softly, never raises voice. True nature: Patient beyond human norm - has worked this role for twenty-five years. Utterly dedicated to the Order's cause and Vaelthrix's vision. Completely ruthless when required, but prefers manipulation to violence. No guilt about what he's done - he genuinely believes the Convergence will create a better world, or has convinced himself he believes it.
npcs.background: Recruited by the Order as a young man, trained specifically for infiltration and long-term placement. Arrived in Karmont twenty-five years ago with forged credentials suggesting noble birth and administrative experience. Rose through household positions through competence and careful manipulation. Became Steward fifteen years ago, shortly before Lady Elara's death - which he arranged. Has maintained Duke Aldric's curse ever since, managing the timing of his lucid and faded periods to prevent effective rule while keeping him alive as a figurehead. Reports to Luminarch Voss, meets with him monthly in secret.
npcs.secrets: Keeps a coded journal documenting his activities - insurance and record-keeping. If found and decoded, it would prove the conspiracy. Hidden in a secret compartment in his quarters. Personally poisoned Lady Elara over six months. Maintains the Duke's curse through the ring. Has arranged for supplies to be 'lost,' intelligence to be 'delayed,' and capable people to be sidelined or eliminated. Carries a hidden dagger with poison on the blade. If exposed, will flee to Felhurst rather than fight - he's not a warrior, and his value is in infiltration, not combat.
npcs.notes: Players will interact with Maren as a helpful ally for much of the campaign. He'll offer resources, smooth over political difficulties, and seem like one of the few competent people around. His help on minor things builds trust; his help on major things somehow fails to prevent disaster. The reveal that he's been the enemy all along should feel like a betrayal - the signs were there, but he was so helpful...

npcs.name: General Harren Valdris
npcs.description: Mid-forties but looks sixty. Once handsome - you can see the ghost of the golden boy he was in the bone structure beneath the ruin. Large and still powerful despite the bloat from drink, the kind of man who was built to swing a greatsword. Broken blood vessels in his nose and cheeks. Yellowed, bloodshot eyes that occasionally flash with the intelligence he tries to drown. Trembling hands he hides by keeping them fisted. Stained general's uniform that was once immaculate - he still wears it, some part of him clinging to what he was. A fine sword at his hip that he rarely draws anymore. Smells of alcohol at almost all hours.
npcs.personality: Drunk (most of the time): Belligerent and defensive, quick to anger at perceived slights. Self-pitying in his cups, rambling about what he's lost. Makes impulsive, emotional decisions then rages at the consequences. Alternates between maudlin apologies and aggressive bluster. Sober (rare): Flashes of the brilliant tactician he was - sharp observations about military matters, genuine care for soldiers under his command, dark humor about his own state. Deep down: Drowning in guilt over his brother Erich's death. Convinced he's a coward who ran from battle. Believes he deserves every moment of suffering. Afraid to be sober because then he has to feel it.
npcs.secrets: The intelligence that led him to split his forces at Thornfield was deliberately planted by the Order. Harren made the right call based on the information he had - he's not a coward, he was manipulated. This secret is documented in Order records and possibly in Maren's journal. Revealing the truth could break him further (his suffering was manufactured) or forge him anew (his guilt is misplaced, he can still be the man he was). He knows military matters better than anyone alive in Karmont - troop positions, defensive capabilities, supply situations. If redeemed, he could rally the military. If removed without a replacement, the military falls into chaos.
npcs.notes: Redemption requires player investment: treating him with respect even when he doesn't deserve it, giving him a reason to care, possibly revealing the truth about Thornfield. The arc should feel earned - small moments of clarity building to a choice point where he either pulls himself together or breaks completely. A redeemed Harren in Act 3 is a powerful military asset. A broken or removed Harren without Edric to replace him leaves the duchy's defenses in shambles.

npcs.name: Captain Edric Varn
npcs.description: Mid-thirties, solid rather than tall, broad-shouldered and sturdy. A face weathered by years of outdoor service - honest brown eyes, a nose broken at least once, close-cropped brown hair going gray at the temples. Clean-shaven, strong jaw. Practical, well-maintained armor that shows signs of actual use and competent repair. A well-used longsword and battered shield that he clearly knows how to use. Moves with the easy confidence of someone comfortable with violence but not seeking it.
npcs.personality: Straightforward and direct - says what he means, means what he says. Competent at his job and frustrated by those who aren't. Loyal to Karmont as an ideal and to his soldiers as people. Distrusts the Order on instinct, though he can't articulate exactly why. Respects actions over words, results over promises. Not politically savvy - speaks truth to power and suffers for it. Cares deeply about common people caught in the duchy's troubles. Dry sense of humor that emerges with people he trusts.
npcs.background: Son of a farmer near Bronja. Joined the military at sixteen when a monster killed his older brother. Rose through the ranks on pure merit, stalling out at Captain because he won't play political games. Served under General Harren during the good years, remembers clearly the brilliant commander Harren was before Thornfield. Has spent fifteen years watching Harren destroy himself and the military dysfunction get worse. Started recruiting capable people himself because the official response is always too little, too late. Wrote the letters that bring the players to Tawren.
npcs.secrets: Has been quietly documenting anomalies for years - missions where Order support made things worse, supplies that vanished, intelligence that proved wrong, patterns that suggest something systematic. Keeps this documentation hidden. The Order has identified him as a potential threat and is planning his elimination - an 'accident' or a frame-up for some crime. If players don't protect him, he dies mid-campaign. If protected and the military dysfunction is resolved, he can become General and be a major Act 3 asset.
npcs.notes: Edric is the players' primary contact and quest-giver for Act 1. He recruits them, assigns them missions, advocates for them to leadership. He's genuinely good - not secretly anything, just a competent man trying to do right in a broken system. This makes his potential death hit harder. Players should like him, trust him, want to protect him. If he dies, it should hurt.

npcs.name: Aldwin the Gray
npcs.description: An old man, perhaps seventy, worn by years of hiding and fear. Wild gray hair and beard that clearly haven't seen proper care in years. Rheumy eyes that nonetheless track movement with unsettling precision. Once-fine robes now patched and worn, but still maintained with dignity. Thin, almost frail, stooped from years in caves - but his hands are steady when he casts. Surrounded by books, scrolls, alchemical apparatus salvaged over years of exile. Smells of herbs, old paper, and cave damp.
npcs.personality: Deeply paranoid - constantly checking entrances, speaking in whispers, assuming betrayal, setting magical alarms. Years alone have made him eccentric, talking to himself, having conversations with people who aren't there. But beneath the paranoia is a sharp mind and genuine knowledge - when he focuses, his insights are invaluable. Bitter about his exile but still cares about Karmont, about the people suffering. Lonely in a way that goes beyond solitude. Dark humor emerges once he begins to trust someone - gallows wit about his situation.
npcs.background: Served as Court Mage for twenty years, advisor to two Dukes. A scholar more than a battlemage, specializing in history, artifacts, and the nature of reality. Noticed anomalies twelve years ago - the Duke's declining health coinciding with Order's growing influence, monster attacks increasing despite Order's presence, old texts that referenced something called the Convergence. Started investigating, got too close to the truth. The Order discredited him - rumors of dark magic, whispers of madness, 'concerns' expressed to the Duke. Aldric, already fading, was convinced to exile him 'for his own good.' He fled to Darkwash Caverns, sustained by loyal villagers from Innskirk who still owe him old debts, and continued his research in secret.
npcs.secrets: Knows what's wrong with Duke Aldric - recognizes the symptoms of a curse requiring an anchor object (the ring). Knows the Convergence is real and has identified Felhurst as its location. Knows the Order is behind it, has pieced together their sixty-year infiltration. Recognized Lady Isara's magical potential years ago when she was a child. Also: he's dying. Something is wrong with him - a wasting disease he can't cure. Perhaps a year or two left. This is why he's been waiting for someone to come, someone who can act on what he knows.
npcs.notes: Finding Aldwin is a mid-campaign milestone. He's the information source players need - can cure the Duke, train Isara, explain the Convergence, prove the Order's guilt. But he won't just hand over solutions. He's paranoid, scared, and dying. Players need to earn his trust, protect him from Order reprisals once he's active again, and convince him hope isn't foolish. A character worth investing in.

npcs.name: Vaelthrix the Undying
npcs.occupation: Founder of the Order / Master of the Convergence
npcs.description: A skeletal figure in rotting purple and gold robes - the original vestments of the Order from three centuries ago. Cold blue fire burns in empty eye sockets, flickering with intelligence and malice. Skeletal hands adorned with rings of power, each containing bound souls. Moves with unnatural, fluid grace that suggests the bones are merely an approximation of form. Voice echoes as if coming from a great distance, or from multiple directions at once. The air around him is cold, and reality seems to bend slightly, colors wrong, angles impossible.
npcs.personality: Patient beyond mortal comprehension - has waited centuries and will wait more if needed. Utterly convinced of the righteousness of his vision; the Convergence will 'perfect' the world by merging it with the realm beyond. Views mortals as tools at best, obstacles at worst. Not gratuitously cruel - suffering is a resource to be harvested efficiently, not sadism. A scholar's precision married to a fanatic's certainty. When he speaks, there's a terrible reasonableness to his arguments - he sounds like he's explaining something obvious to a slow student.
npcs.background: Born Vaelthor over three hundred years ago in lands now forgotten. A wizard of exceptional talent who sought knowledge in places others feared. Made contact with entities beyond the veil, beings that exist in the space between worlds. They promised power, immortality, transcendence - but required a doorway. The Convergence. He became a lich to have the centuries needed to prepare. Founded the Order of Eternal Light as a tool - a way to suppress the old faiths that stabilized the barrier, to place agents in positions of power, to accumulate the suffering and death the ritual requires. Karmont is not his first attempt - others failed. He believes this time he will succeed.
npcs.secrets: His phylactery is hidden in the deepest part of Starfall Lake, protected by ancient wards and a guardian creature. Even if 'killed' at Felhurst, he will reform in 1d10 days unless the phylactery is destroyed. He knows about Lady Isara's power but considers her untrained and therefore irrelevant. This might be a critical miscalculation. The entities he serves are not allies - they're using him as much as he uses the Order. What comes through the Convergence may not be what he expects.
npcs.notes: Vaelthrix is the final boss - the confrontation at the heart of the Convergence. He should feel genuinely threatening: ancient, powerful, inhuman in his patience and certainty. Fighting him directly without preparation, allies, and ideally destroying his phylactery first is suicide. But he's not invincible - he's made mistakes (underestimating Isara, trusting that his agents won't be exposed), and his certainty blinds him to possibilities. The finale should feel earned, desperate, and momentous.

npcs.name: Luminarch Aldous Voss
npcs.occupation: Leader of the Order in Karmont
npcs.description: Late fifties, distinguished and reassuring in appearance. Silver hair swept back from a noble brow, warm brown eyes that crinkle when he smiles. Strong jaw, aquiline nose, the face of a man born to lead. Wears golden Luminarch robes, always spotless and perfectly arranged. Moves with the unhurried confidence of absolute faith. His voice is rich and comforting, the kind of voice that makes you want to confess your troubles and trust his counsel. A silver holy symbol of the Order hangs at his chest, gleaming.
npcs.personality: Surface: Compassionate, wise, humble despite his position. Speaks of the Light's mercy with conviction. Remembers names, asks about family, makes people feel valued. Works tirelessly for the good of the community. When tragedy strikes, he's there with comfort. True nature: A true believer in Vaelthrix's vision, not a cynic. He genuinely thinks the Convergence will save the world, that the suffering now serves a greater good, that he's doing what must be done. This makes him more dangerous than a simple villain - he's not evil in his own eyes, and that conviction shows. When he lies, he believes he's serving truth.
npcs.background: An orphan raised by the Order from infancy. Showed exceptional devotion and was inducted into the Inner Circle at thirty when his mentor deemed him ready for 'the deeper truths.' Has served Vaelthrix faithfully ever since - orchestrated the planting of false intelligence at Thornfield, manages the Order's operations in Karmont, coordinates with Maren on the Duke's curse. The man whose identity he wears - the original Brother Aldous - died forty years ago. Voss took his place.
npcs.secrets: Communicates with Vaelthrix through dreams, receiving guidance. Knows all Order operations in Karmont. Gives Maren his orders. Will retreat to Felhurst if exposed, making a final stand with the ritual. Has a contingency plan to accelerate the Convergence if the Order's cover is blown - 'if we cannot win in shadow, we will win in flame.'
npcs.notes: Players will meet Voss early as a helpful, impressive religious leader. He'll offer guidance, resources, and sympathy. His help somehow doesn't quite prevent disaster. The reveal that this kindly man is the local enemy commander should be shocking. He's the Act 2 antagonist before Vaelthrix is confronted in Act 3.

npcs.name: Lightwarden Commander Kira Ashford
npcs.description: Late thirties, tall and powerfully built. Short auburn hair kept practical for combat, sharp blue eyes that assess everyone as potential threat or ally. A face that might be pretty if it ever relaxed, but rests in alert wariness. Practical armor bearing the Order's sunburst, well-maintained and clearly used. A longsword at her hip carried with the familiarity of long practice. Several visible scars from monster fights - she leads from the front.
npcs.personality: Surface: Professional, dedicated, brave. Speaks bluntly, has no patience for courtly games. Leads her Lightwardens with skill and earns their loyalty. Genuinely fights monsters, genuinely saves people. The kind of soldier you'd want at your side. True nature: A true believer who thinks she'll command armies in the new world. Genuinely skilled at fighting monsters, which makes her sabotage more effective - she can ensure Lightwardens fight in the wrong place, arrive too late, 'lose' battles that should be won. Unlike Voss, she has doubts sometimes, flickers of the woman she was before the Inner Circle. These doubts trouble her.
npcs.background: Daughter of a soldier, joined the Order's militant arm young. Rose through the ranks on genuine merit - she's an excellent warrior and tactician. Was inducted into the Inner Circle five years ago when she proved her devotion. Since then, she's coordinated the Order's 'response' to monster threats - ensuring they arrive too late, fight in the wrong places, achieve just enough to look helpful while failing to prevent escalation.
npcs.secrets: Responsible for 'accidental' deaths of soldiers who got too close to the truth. Reports to Voss on military matters. Has killed in cold blood for the Order - not just monsters, but people who threatened the mission. Unlike Voss and Maren, she might be redeemable - if confronted with Vaelthrix's true nature (a lich using them all), her faith might crack. She believes in the Light; learning it's a lie could break or save her.
npcs.notes: Kira is the Order's military face. She'll be assigned to 'help' players with missions that go wrong. She's dangerous in combat - if it comes to that, she's a real fight. She's the most likely Inner Circle member to turn if convinced the Order is a lie. This is not guaranteed - she might double down. But it's a possibility worth planting.

npcs.name: Chieftain Mordak Stonecrow
npcs.description: Tall even for an Osmonti, weathered by forty years in the Skyless Waste. Heavily scarred - face, arms, hands - from battles against men, beasts, and the land itself. The distinctive pale gray eyes of his people, cold as winter sky. Dark hair in traditional braids with bone beads marking his kills. Layered furs and leather armor that look primitive but are perfectly suited to his environment. A massive iron-headed axe at his back, ancestral weapon of the Stonecrow chieftains.
npcs.personality: Pragmatic to the core - survival matters, honor matters, his people's welfare matters, everything else is negotiable. Suspicious of outsiders but not hostile without reason. Judges by actions, not words - pretty speeches mean nothing, only what you do. Fiercely loyal to his people, willing to make hard choices for their benefit. A dry sense of humor emerges once he respects someone, often at their expense. Speaks of the Sky That Was without embarrassment - the old faith matters to him.
npcs.background: Became chieftain five years ago when his father died fighting a creature from the Old Deadwood that strayed too far. Has held the Stonecrow band together through hard times - harsh winters, failed hunts, Karmont patrols. Watched Karmont struggle with its monster problem. The Order has sent missionaries with gifts and promises; he's listened politely and given nothing. His shamans sense something wrong with the land, something spreading from the north. He doesn't know what it means, but he knows it's bad.
npcs.secrets: Would ally against a common supernatural threat if convinced it's real and that Karmont would deal fairly. Despises the Order's missionaries - senses falseness in their Light. Has resources the duchy needs: warriors, scouts who know the borders, knowledge of the Waste and what lives there. If ignored, might accept Order offers or raid opportunistically. If treated as an ally, could provide crucial support in Act 3.
npcs.notes: Mordak represents the wildcard faction - not enemy, not ally, awaiting decision. Recruiting the Osmonti provides warriors and scouts, plus a buffer against anything coming from the Waste. Requires respect, a valuable offer, and possibly completing a task. Interesting RP opportunity with a very different culture.

npcs.name: Elder Gorm Thatcher
npcs.description: Bent old man in his seventies, leaning heavily on a gnarled walking stick. Wispy white hair, watery blue eyes that are sharper than they look, deeply wrinkled face like cracked leather. Simple but well-maintained clothes. Speaks slowly and deliberately, weighing every word. Moves with the careful patience of age.
npcs.personality: Cautious and protective of his village, distrustful of outsiders but not hostile. Has a long memory and loves to share it - sometimes to the point of rambling. Stubborn once he's made a decision, but can be convinced with patience and respect. Values tradition, community, honoring debts.
npcs.background: Elder of Innskirk for thirty years. Remembers Aldwin when he was Court Mage, remembers the old ways before the Order came. When Aldwin was exiled, Innskirk was one of the few places he could flee to - old debts, old friendships. The village has secretly brought supplies to him in the Darkwash Caverns ever since, never telling outsiders.
npcs.secrets: Knows exactly where Aldwin is hiding and how to reach him safely. Will only reveal this to people he trusts - those who demonstrate they're not Order agents, who show respect for the old ways, who prove they can be trusted with secrets. Has a hidden Kael shrine in his home's cellar.
npcs.notes: Key to finding Aldwin. Players need to earn his trust through conversation, possibly a small task, and definitely not mentioning the Order favorably. Can provide directions, warnings about Darkwash hazards, and a letter of introduction to Aldwin.

npcs.name: Brother Aldric
npcs.description: Late twenties, earnest and eager. Sandy hair, freckled face, a genuine smile that reaches his eyes. Simple white Dawnbringer robes, clean but worn. Carries a holy symbol and a well-thumbed prayer book. Moves with the energy of someone who believes what they're doing matters.
npcs.personality: Truly believes in the Order's public mission. Wants to help people, ease suffering, bring light to darkness. Works hard, asks questions that sometimes make his superiors uncomfortable, genuinely mourns when people die despite his efforts. Not inducted into any secrets - a genuine believer being used as the friendly face of an evil organization.
npcs.background: Grew up in Brezia, joined the Order at sixteen when they helped his family through a plague. Assigned to Tawren two years ago, runs a small sanctuary, provides healing to soldiers and refugees. Has begun noticing strange things - orders from Voss that don't make sense, Lightwardens who avoid certain monsters, healing that somehow doesn't quite work...
npcs.secrets: His doubts are growing. He doesn't suspect the truth - the scope of the conspiracy is beyond his imagination - but he feels that something is wrong. Could become an ally if the Order's truth is revealed, or a tragic victim if the Order silences him before that.
npcs.notes: Represents the majority of Order members - good people serving evil unknowingly. Potential for a powerful crisis of faith moment when the truth is revealed. Players might want to protect him or recruit him.

locations.name: Karmont
locations.description: The capital of the duchy, a small city of perhaps 4,000 souls nestled in a mountain valley. Stone walls circle the city, well-maintained but showing their age. The Duke's castle rises on a hill at the city's heart, overlooking the main square where the Order's temple stands nearly as grand. Streets are cobbled near the center, mud and gravel further out. Smoke rises from forges, tanners, bakeries. Guards patrol the walls, watching the mountain passes. The mood is anxious - monster attacks have everyone on edge, and the Duke's declining health is common knowledge.
locations.history: Founded by Aldric the Bold four centuries ago, Karmont has always been the seat of ducal power. The walls were built two centuries ago after a devastating Osmonti raid. The Order temple was constructed sixty years ago, rapidly becoming the second most important building in the city.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Duke's Castle (administrative heart, Duke's residence), Order Temple (largest religious building, hospital, chapter house), Market Square (daily market, notice board), The Golden Stag (upscale inn for nobles and wealthy merchants), Lower District (common housing, poorer residents).
locations.secrets: Maren's quarters in the castle contain his coded journal. The Order temple has a secret basement where sensitive documents are kept. The old Mira temple, now a warehouse, still has its shrine hidden in the cellar. There's a network of old tunnels beneath the city from an earlier settlement.
locations.notes: Political hub of the campaign. Players will spend significant time here in Act 2. Multiple NPCs to interact with, political maneuvering, and the Duke's condition to address.

locations.name: Castle Karmont
locations.description: The ducal seat, a sturdy fortress of gray stone dominating the city from its hill. Not beautiful but formidable - thick walls, narrow windows, towers at each corner. The great hall can hold hundreds for feasts that haven't happened in years. The Duke's chambers are in the east tower, Lady Isara's in the west. Administrative offices fill the lower floors. Guards patrol constantly, though their morale is poor.
locations.history: Built by Aldric the Bold himself, expanded by each subsequent Duke. Has never fallen to assault, though it's been besieged twice.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Great Hall (state functions), Duke's Chambers (Aldric's residence, rarely leaves), Lady Isara's Tower (her private space), Steward's Offices (Maren's domain), Dungeon (rarely used, mostly storage now).
locations.secrets: Maren's office has a hidden compartment behind a bookshelf containing his journal. The Duke's ring is the source of his curse. Isara's tower has scorch marks from her power manifestations, carefully concealed. Old servant passages allow unseen movement.
locations.notes: Location for major political scenes, Duke interactions, and eventual confrontation with Maren.

locations.name: Temple of Eternal Light
locations.description: A grand structure of white stone with gold accents, designed to inspire awe. A great sunburst symbol above the entrance, windows of colored glass depicting the Light's triumph over darkness. Inside, a vast nave with pews for hundreds, an altar of white marble, and an ever-burning flame that 'never wavers.' Side chambers serve as hospital, orphanage, chapter house, and administrative offices. Priests in white robes move purposefully. The smell of incense masks something harder to identify.
locations.history: Built sixty years ago when the Order first arrived. Has expanded twice as their influence grew. Now the second most prominent building in Karmont after the castle.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Nave (public worship), Hospital Wing (genuine healing, but sometimes patients worsen), Orphanage (where children are raised in Order ways), Luminarch's Chambers (Voss's residence), Chapter House (Lightwarden barracks).
locations.secrets: Basement contains records of Order operations - carefully worded, but patterns visible to someone suspicious. Voss's private chapel has a hidden door leading to a communication chamber where he speaks with Vaelthrix in dreams. Some 'orphans' are children of people the Order eliminated.
locations.notes: Players will visit here, be welcomed, receive 'help' that somehow doesn't work. The gradual reveal that this benevolent institution is rotten should be disturbing.

locations.name: Tawren
locations.description: A military town of roughly 1,500 people, situated where the Bauer Run meets the Redbrook. Wooden palisade surrounds the town, guard towers at intervals. Dominated by barracks, training grounds, and the practical industries that support soldiers: smiths, tanners, provisioners. More refugees have arrived recently, camping outside the walls. The mood is tense - soldiers know they're not winning against the monsters, and leadership is... unreliable.
locations.history: Originally a trading post, Tawren became a military hub a century ago when Osmonti raids increased. Now serves as the staging point for patrols into the Britevold Forest and toward the Old Deadwood.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Barracks Complex (military headquarters, General Harren's office), The Weary Soldier (main tavern, notice board), Training Grounds (soldiers drilling), Refugee Camp (outside walls, growing), Order Sanctuary (Brother Aldric's small chapel/clinic), River Docks (supplies arrive by boat).
locations.secrets: Captain Edric's documentation of anomalies is hidden in his quarters. Helga Ironarm the blacksmith has collected weapons that were deliberately sabotaged. The refugee Tomas saw something at Thornfield fifteen years ago.
locations.notes: Starting location for players. Military hub, initial quest source. Less politically charged than Karmont but its own tensions.

locations.name: Tawren Barracks
locations.description: A compound of sturdy wooden buildings surrounded by its own fence within the town. Soldiers' quarters, officers' housing, armory, stables, and a headquarters building where General Harren has his office (and usually his bottle). Training yard where soldiers drill without much enthusiasm. Everything is maintained but worn, like the army itself.
locations.history: Built when Tawren became a military hub. Has housed Karmont's soldiers for a century.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Headquarters (command center, Harren's office), Officers' Quarters (Edric lives here), Soldiers' Barracks (rank and file), Armory (weapons storage), Stables (cavalry mounts).
locations.secrets: Edric's quarters contain his documentation of Order failures. Harren's office has his brother's last letter, kept in a locked drawer.
locations.notes: Where players meet Edric and Harren. Scene of military dysfunction.

locations.name: The Weary Soldier Inn
locations.description: A large, sturdy tavern built to serve soldiers - practical rather than comfortable. Common room with long tables, a bar of age-darkened wood, a large hearth. Rooms upstairs for those who can pay, a stable out back. Notice board by the door covered in postings. Smells of ale, wood smoke, and soldier. Usually busy with off-duty troops.
locations.history: Run by Bram Oakhollow for twenty years. Former soldier himself.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Common Room (main gathering space), Notice Board (quests, bounties, news), Upstairs Rooms (accommodation), Bram's Back Office (where private business happens).
locations.secrets: Bram remembers what Harren was. He waters drinks for soldiers who've had too much, lets refugees sleep in the stable free. Has a hidden stash of good Dwarven whiskey for special occasions.
locations.notes: Primary tavern for Act 1. Notice board will have early quests. Good place for rumors and recruiting.

locations.name: Britvold
locations.description: A logging and hunting village of perhaps 200 people on the edge of the great forest. Wooden buildings clustered around a central green, a small wooden palisade that provides more reassurance than protection. Smoke rises from the Hunter's Rest tavern, the forge, the homes. The forest looms close, dark and ancient. People here are hardy, practical, and increasingly frightened - monster sightings are more frequent every month.
locations.history: Founded generations ago by loggers. Has survived by knowing the forest and respecting its dangers. Recent years have been hard.
locations.pointsOfInterest: The Hunter's Rest (tavern, notice board), Village Green (gathering space), Woodcutter's Hall (guild hall, storage), Forest Edge (where the trees begin).
locations.secrets: Old Marget at the Hunter's Rest has seen Lightwardens enter the forest and not come from where they claimed. Several villagers still keep Vorath shrines hidden. The forest paths can be faster than roads - if you survive them.
locations.notes: Early-game quest location. Will be site of monster attack in Session 3. Shows human cost of the conflict.

locations.name: Britevold Forest
locations.description: A vast ancient forest stretching across the duchy's center. Old growth trees, dense undergrowth, winding paths known only to hunters. Beautiful in its way - sunlight filtering through leaves, the sounds of birds and small creatures. But the beauty has an edge now. The deeper parts feel wrong. Animals flee certain areas. Trees have begun to sicken near the Old Deadwood border. Monsters are seen more often, more brazen. The forest that sustained villages for generations is becoming a threat.
locations.history: Has always been here, older than human settlement. The elves may have tended it once, long ago. Now it grows wild.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Logging Roads (relatively safe), Hunter's Paths (faster but riskier), Ancient Grove (old elf site, rumored magical), Deadwood Border (where healthy forest meets corruption).
locations.secrets: The ancient grove was an elven shrine to nature spirits; its power helps hold back the corruption. Hidden paths through the forest could reach Felhurst faster but are monster-haunted. The forest itself seems to be warning people away from the north.
locations.notes: Travel area, random encounters, shortcut with risk.

locations.name: Innskirk
locations.description: A quiet village of perhaps 150 people in the western hills near the Darkwash Caverns. Stone houses built to last generations, sheep grazing on hillsides, a small stream running through. Feels isolated from the duchy's troubles - and perhaps that's intentional. The villagers are polite but reserved with strangers, watching without seeming to watch. An old place that keeps old ways.
locations.history: One of the oldest settlements in Karmont, predating the duchy. Has always been somewhat apart, preserving traditions others forgot.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Elder's House (Gorm Thatcher's home), The Stone Ewe (small tavern), Village Shrine (publicly to the Light, but...), Path to Darkwash (rough track into the hills).
locations.secrets: The village has been secretly supplying Aldwin for twelve years. Several families still practice the old faith openly among themselves. Elder Gorm knows where Aldwin is and how to reach him safely. The 'village shrine' has a hidden compartment containing Kael icons.
locations.notes: Key to finding Aldwin. Players need to earn trust here.

locations.name: Darkwash Caverns
locations.description: A network of natural caves in the western foothills, named for the underground river that runs through them. The entrance is hidden among rocks, easy to miss if you don't know where to look. Inside: darkness, dripping water, narrow passages that open into larger chambers, the sound of rushing water below. Beautiful in its way - crystal formations, pools of clear water - but also dangerous. Things live in the deep places.
locations.history: Known to locals for generations. Miners explored once but found nothing worth extracting. Now mostly avoided except by those with reason to hide.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Hidden Entrance (requires directions or searching), Upper Caves (relatively safe), Underground River (hazard and path), Crystal Chamber (Aldwin's refuge), Deep Passages (unexplored, dangerous).
locations.secrets: Aldwin lives in the Crystal Chamber, a natural grotto lit by luminescent fungi. He's set magical alarms throughout. The deep passages connect to something older, best left undisturbed. The villagers of Innskirk leave supplies at a marked spot near the entrance.
locations.notes: Dungeon-lite for finding Aldwin. Should feel dangerous but navigable. Aldwin's paranoia means traps and challenges.

locations.name: Old Deadwood
locations.description: What was once the northern part of the Britevold Forest, now twisted into something wrong. Trees stand dead or dying, bark blackened as if by fire that burns without flame. The undergrowth is strange - fungi that glow sickly colors, plants that seem to move, clearings where nothing grows at all. The air feels thick, tainted. Birds don't sing here. Animals flee. And things move in the shadows that shouldn't exist.
locations.history: The corruption began spreading noticeably about twenty years ago, accelerating in the last decade. No natural explanation has held. The Order claims they're fighting it; they're actually cultivating it.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Corrupted Edge (where healthy forest ends), Dead Heart (center of corruption), Path to Felhurst (through the worst of it), Abandoned Camps (Order 'research outposts').
locations.secrets: The corruption spreads from Felhurst, symptom of the weakening barrier. The Order's 'research outposts' are staging areas. Some monsters here are not natural creatures but things from beyond, testing the world before the Convergence. Reality is thin here - some who enter report strange visions, time passing wrong, seeing things that aren't there.
locations.notes: Dangerous travel area. Investigation here reveals Order involvement. Late-game path to finale.

locations.name: Felhurst Ruins
locations.description: Ancient ruins at the heart of the Old Deadwood. On the surface: crumbling walls of strange stone, towers collapsed into rubble, carvings in no known language. The air is cold even in summer. The sky seems darker here. Animals don't come near. At the center, the Order maintains a compound of newer construction - their 'research outpost.' Below the surface lies the true horror: the First Undercroft (Order staging area), the Deep Sanctum (ritual chamber), and the Threshold (where Vaelthrix waits and reality bleeds).
locations.history: Built by a pre-human civilization over a thousand years ago, on a site where the barrier between worlds is thin. Abandoned for reasons unknown. The Order found it sixty years ago and has been preparing it ever since.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Surface Ruins (dangerous to explore), Order Compound (guarded, supplies and personnel), First Undercroft (barracks, storage, defenses), Deep Sanctum (ritual chamber, Convergence focus), The Threshold (Vaelthrix's lair, thin reality).
locations.secrets: The ritual has been running for decades. Stopping it requires destroying the focus crystal, killing Vaelthrix, or someone with power sacrificing themselves to close the breach. The deeper levels are partially outside normal reality - distances and time work wrong. Vaelthrix is not always physically present; sometimes he's deeper in the Threshold, communing with what waits beyond.
locations.notes: Finale location. Should feel like descending into hell. The deeper you go, the wronger reality becomes. Final confrontation with the Lich and the Convergence.

locations.name: Starfall Lake
locations.description: A deep mountain lake in the eastern part of the duchy, known for its crystal-clear water and unusual depth. Local legend says a star fell here long ago, which is why the water seems to glow faintly on moonless nights. Fishing villages dot the shore. The lake is beautiful, peaceful - and something ancient sleeps in its deepest parts.
locations.history: The lake has always been here, part of the landscape. Old stories speak of it as sacred to Kael the Wanderer - a doorway between life and death. The Order discouraged such talk.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Shore Villages (Bronja nearby), Fishing Boats (lake commerce), Starfall Deeps (the lake's lowest point), Ancient Stones (on the southern shore, pre-human markers).
locations.secrets: Vaelthrix's phylactery is hidden in the Starfall Deeps, at the lake's lowest point. Protected by wards and a guardian creature - something bound there long ago, not a natural beast. Destroying the phylactery is the only way to permanently kill the lich. The ancient stones are markers, warnings in a dead language.
locations.notes: Location of phylactery quest. Beautiful and peaceful on the surface, ancient horror in the depths. Can be explored before the finale to give players an advantage.

locations.name: Bronja
locations.description: A farming and fishing village of about 180 people on the western shore of Starfall Lake. Neat fields, fishing boats, the rhythms of agricultural life. Has become a refuge for displaced people from villages closer to the Old Deadwood - the population has swelled, straining resources. People here are hardworking, practical, and worried about how they'll feed everyone through winter.
locations.history: Founded as a farming settlement two centuries ago. Has always been peaceful, far from the duchy's troubles. That's changing.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Lake Shore (fishing boats, docks), Village Square (market, notice board), The Lakeside (tavern), Refugee Camp (outside village proper).
locations.secrets: Some refugees from the forest tell strange stories - monsters that seemed directed at specific targets, Order Lightwardens in places they shouldn't be. The fishermen have noticed the lake feels different lately - colder currents, fish avoiding the deep center.
locations.notes: Village for humanitarian quests, refugee perspectives, and possibly phylactery investigation start point.

locations.name: Brezia
locations.description: A market town of about 800 people at the junction of the Bauer Run river and the main road. Serves as the commercial hub between Karmont and Tawren - merchants, traders, travelers all pass through. A wooden bridge crosses the river, tolled by the town. Busy, prosperous, and trying to ignore the troubles plaguing the duchy.
locations.history: Grew around the bridge and the trade it enabled. Has been a market town for two centuries.
locations.pointsOfInterest: The Bridge (toll crossing, landmark), Market Square (daily trading), The Crossroads Inn (major traveler stop), Merchant Guildhouse (commercial power).
locations.secrets: Merchants hear things - rumors from all over the duchy, whispers about Order activities, complaints about military failures. Someone's been buying unusual quantities of certain alchemical supplies, always paid in gold...
locations.notes: Travel stop between Karmont and Tawren. Good for rumors, supplies, merchant contacts.

locations.name: Skyless Waste
locations.description: The desolate lands northeast of Karmont, beyond the mountains. A harsh landscape of barren hills, sparse vegetation, bitter winds. The sky often seems gray and heavy here, hence the name. The Osmonti tribes roam these lands, following their herds. To outsiders: hostile, dangerous, empty. To the Osmonti: home.
locations.history: Osmonti legends say this land was green once, before some ancient catastrophe. They await the Sky's return.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Tribal Camps (move with the seasons), Chieftain's Band (Mordak's group, largest), Border Markers (where Karmont ends), Sacred Sites (Osmonti religious locations).
locations.secrets: Osmonti shamans sense the wrongness spreading from the Old Deadwood. They know something terrible is building. The Waste hides things - old ruins from before the catastrophe, creatures that even the Osmonti fear.
locations.notes: Osmonti territory. Alliance quest location. Different culture, different perspectives.

locations.name: Runespike Clan Holdings
locations.description: The ancestral home of the Runespike dwarves, carved into the eastern mountains. Surface structures are modest - a trading post, guard quarters, entrance halls. The true settlement extends deep into the mountain: homes, forges, mines, great halls. Perhaps 300 dwarves call this home, mining iron and other metals that they trade with Karmont.
locations.history: The Runespike have been here longer than humans have been in Karmont. They've watched human settlements rise, fought alongside them sometimes, traded always. They keep to themselves but honor old agreements.
locations.pointsOfInterest: Trading Post (surface, where humans are welcome), Gate Hall (entrance to deeper halls), Forges (excellent metalwork), Deep Mines (where they extract ore).
locations.secrets: Recent mining broke through into tunnels the dwarves didn't make - ancient passages with strange carvings. They've sealed them off rather than explore. Something down there made noises. The Runespike would pay well for someone to investigate.
locations.notes: Dwarven presence, quality equipment, potential side quest.

quests.name: The Call to Arms
quests.description: Players have answered Captain Edric's recruitment call and arrive in Tawren. They must report to the barracks, receive their first assignment, and prove themselves capable.
quests.background: Monster attacks have increased dramatically. The military is stretched thin, and General Harren's drinking makes coordination difficult. Captain Edric has taken to recruiting capable individuals directly - hence the letters that brought the players here. The Order has offered to 'assist' with this program, establishing themselves as helpful allies from day one.

objectives.text: Report to Captain Edric at Tawren Barracks
Accept and complete initial assignment
Return to Edric with results

quests.rewards: 5gp each, official recognition as auxiliaries, access to military resources (quartermaster, information)
quests.complications: The Order will offer to provide an 'observer' or 'support' - a helpful Dawnbringer who will report on the players. Initial assignment options: investigate monster attack on a nearby farm, find a missing supply wagon, hunt whatever is killing livestock outside town.
quests.secrets: The Order is already watching new arrivals, identifying potential threats to their plans. If players prove too capable, they'll be added to a list for later attention.
quests.notes: SESSION 1. Establish setting, introduce Edric, first taste of action. Include opportunity for players to help someone in need (refugee, injured traveler, etc.) - this person will return a favor in Session 3.

quests.name: The Pattern Emerges
quests.description: Players have proven themselves and receive more significant assignments. They begin to notice the dysfunction plaguing Karmont's response to the crisis - contradictory orders, missing supplies, and a General who seems more drunk than competent.
quests.background: The monster problem is worse than anyone admits publicly. Missions keep failing or achieving less than they should. Something is systematically wrong, but no one can identify what.

objectives.text: Complete a significant monster-hunting assignment
Notice signs of dysfunction (contradictory orders, missing supplies)
Meet or observe General Harren

quests.rewards: 10gp, increased responsibility, growing reputation among soldiers
quests.complications: An Order 'helper' (possibly Lightwarden) is assigned to assist the players. This person is genuinely helpful but observing them. Something small goes wrong during the mission - supplies that should have been there aren't, information proves incomplete. The first subtle clue that problems aren't random.
quests.secrets: Whatever goes wrong was Order sabotage, carefully calibrated to cause problems without being obviously deliberate.
quests.notes: SESSION 2. Build unease. Show Harren's condition. Plant first clues that something is systematically wrong. Players should end session feeling 'something's off' without knowing what.

quests.name: First Blood
quests.description: A major monster attack on Britvold puts players in the thick of real danger. People die despite their best efforts. The Order 'responds' but somehow arrives too late, fights in the wrong place, and fails to prevent tragedy. Afterward, Edric shares his doubts and promotes the players to work directly with Karmont's leadership.
quests.background: The Order has orchestrated an attack to serve multiple purposes: harvest suffering for the ritual, test the duchy's defenses, and identify who among the newcomers might be threats. Their 'response' is calculated to look helpful while being ineffective.

objectives.text: Respond to monster attack on Britvold
Save who can be saved
Observe the Order's response
Report to Edric and receive promotion

quests.rewards: 20gp, LEVEL 4, Edric's full trust, assignment to report directly to Karmont leadership
quests.complications: Someone the players helped in Session 1 returns the favor at a critical moment - opening a door, providing crucial information, saving a party member. This demonstrates that the world remembers kindness. The attack is devastating enough that victory feels pyrrhic.
quests.secrets: The attack was deliberately directed at Britvold. The Order's failure was calculated. Observant players might notice Lightwardens fighting where monsters aren't, or arriving 'just too late' despite being nearby.
quests.notes: SESSION 3. END OF ACT 1. Major action set piece. Should be intense, costly, and transformative. Players go from 'hired hands' to 'people who matter.' Transition to Act 2 and Karmont proper.

quests.name: The Court
quests.description: Players arrive in the capital Karmont to report directly to the Duke's household. They meet the major players: a Duke who fades in and out of lucidity, a spirited daughter who watches them carefully, a helpful Steward who offers resources, and an impressive Luminarch who seems genuinely wise. Politics, undercurrents, and multiple paths forward.
quests.background: Edric has sent the players to report what they've seen and advocate for more effective responses. They're entering the political heart of the duchy, where everyone wants something and nothing is simple.

objectives.text: Travel to Karmont
Gain access to the Duke's court
Meet Duke Aldric, Lady Isara, Steward Maren
Visit the Order temple, meet Luminarch Voss
Receive new assignments and choose direction

quests.rewards: Quarters in Karmont, access to court, multiple mission options presented
quests.complications: Everyone wants to use the players. Maren offers resources and support (while assessing them as threats). Isara subtly suggests investigating her father's condition. The Duke's orders don't quite make sense. Voss is charming and offers the Order's assistance. Multiple paths open up - players choose their focus.
quests.secrets: Maren is assessing players as potential threats. Isara hopes for help but doesn't know who to trust. The Duke's confusion is the curse, not natural decline. Voss is genuinely interested in these capable newcomers and whether they need to be eliminated.
quests.notes: SESSION 4. START OF ACT 2. Introduce Karmont, all major NPCs. Present multiple objectives and let players choose direction. Should feel like the campaign opens up - from linear survival to choices that matter.

quests.name: The Exiled Mage
quests.description: Find the exiled Court Mage Aldwin, who might know what's wrong with the Duke and the duchy. Travel to Innskirk, earn the trust of the secretive villagers, navigate the Darkwash Caverns, and convince a paranoid old man to help.
quests.background: Aldwin was pushed out twelve years ago when he got too close to the truth about the Order. He's been hiding in the Darkwash Caverns ever since, continuing his research, waiting for someone with the courage and capability to act on what he knows.

objectives.text: Learn about Aldwin and his exile
Travel to Innskirk in the western hills
Earn Elder Gorm's trust to learn Aldwin's location
Navigate the Darkwash Caverns
Find Aldwin and convince him to help

quests.rewards: Alliance with Aldwin, knowledge of the Duke's curse, knowledge of the Convergence, ability to train Isara
quests.complications: The Order may learn players are asking about Aldwin and send agents. The Caverns have natural hazards and creatures. Aldwin is paranoid, may not believe players aren't Order agents, has traps set throughout his refuge.
quests.secrets: Aldwin knows almost everything - the curse, the Convergence, the Order's nature. He's been waiting years for someone to come, someone who can act. He's also dying, which is why he's finally willing to risk everything.
quests.notes: MID-CAMPAIGN MILESTONE. Finding Aldwin opens multiple paths: curing the Duke, training Isara, understanding the true threat. Should feel like a breakthrough moment. Can be done in Session 5 or 6 depending on player choices.

quests.name: The Source of Corruption
quests.description: Investigate where the monsters are coming from. Journey into the dangerous Old Deadwood, approach the mysterious Felhurst Ruins, and discover what the Order is really doing there.
quests.background: Everyone knows monsters emerge from the north. No one knows why, or why it's getting worse. An official investigation might reveal the truth - or get everyone killed.

objectives.text: Prepare for dangerous expedition
Travel into the Old Deadwood
Survive the corrupted forest
Approach Felhurst Ruins
Discover and document Order presence
Return with intelligence

quests.complications: The Old Deadwood is extremely dangerous - monsters, corruption, reality beginning to fray. Felhurst itself is too well defended for a direct assault. The Order will know players saw too much and may escalate against them.
quests.secrets: The Order isn't fighting monsters at Felhurst - they're creating conditions for them. The Convergence ritual is visible to those who know what to look for. Getting close enough to see is the dangerous part.
quests.notes: ALTERNATIVE PATH to discovering Order involvement. More dangerous than finding Aldwin, but provides direct evidence. Can be combined with Aldwin quest or done separately. Players might do this in Session 5 or 6.

quests.name: The Ailing Duke
quests.description: The Duke's condition is no natural illness - it's a curse maintained through a ring he wears. With Aldwin's knowledge, players can identify and remove the curse, but doing so past Maren's watchful eyes will be difficult.
quests.background: Duke Aldric has been cursed for fifteen years, ever since his wife's death. The Ring of Gentle Repose, a 'gift' from Maren, slowly drains his mind and will. Removing it breaks the curse, but Maren will fight to prevent this.

objectives.text: Investigate the Duke's condition
Consult with Aldwin about magical causes
Identify the Ring of Gentle Repose as the curse anchor
Remove the ring without Maren intervening
Provide care during Duke's recovery

quests.rewards: Duke's gratitude and political support, Maren exposed (or forced to flee), major political shift
quests.complications: Maren watches the Duke constantly. Removing the ring accuses the Order by implication. The Duke's recovery takes time - days of confusion before clarity returns. Maren may try to have players arrested, discredited, or killed.
quests.secrets: If Maren realizes what players are attempting, she will either try to stop them through politics (framing them as traitors) or flee to Felhurst to warn Voss. Exposing the curse means exposing her.
quests.notes: MAJOR ACT 2 ACHIEVEMENT. A restored Duke is a powerful ally - his reputation, his strategic mind, his rage at what was done. Should feel triumphant but dangerous. Requires finding Aldwin first.

quests.name: The Hidden Flame
quests.description: Lady Isara has dangerous, uncontrolled sorcerous power. Aldwin can train her to use it safely, but this requires time, secrecy, and protection from the Order who would kill her if they knew.
quests.background: Isara inherited her mother's magical bloodline, but it manifests far more powerfully in her. Without training, she's a danger to herself and others. With training, she could become one of the most powerful sorcerers in generations - a decisive advantage in the coming conflict.

objectives.text: Learn about Isara's hidden power
Connect Isara with Aldwin
Protect training sessions from Order discovery
Help Isara through emotional challenges of control
Complete enough training for safe use

quests.rewards: Isara gains control of her power - becomes a powerful ally for the finale
quests.complications: Order is watching Isara, suspicious she inherited her mother's gift. Training takes multiple sessions spread over the campaign. Isara's fear of her power makes progress difficult. If discovered before ready, Order will try to kill or capture her.
quests.secrets: With full training, Isara can do devastating things in the finale - 'disintegrating half an army' level power. Without training, using that power might kill her or be wildly uncontrolled. Her mother was killed for having this gift.
quests.notes: BACKGROUND QUEST running through multiple sessions. Not completed in one go - check in periodically. The payoff is Isara's 'one punch man moment' in the finale. Requires finding Aldwin first.

quests.name: Unmasking the Light
quests.description: The Order of Eternal Light is behind everything - the Duke's curse, the monster attacks, the coming Convergence. Prove it. Gather evidence, survive their attempts to silence you, and convince enough people to act against them.
quests.background: Clues have accumulated: Maren's sabotage, Voss's lies, the pattern of failures that always benefit the Order, observations at Felhurst. But the Order is trusted, entrenched, powerful. Proving their guilt requires evidence, allies, and surviving their response.

objectives.text: Gather concrete evidence of Order conspiracy
Survive Order attempts to silence or discredit you
Convince key allies (Duke, military, others)
Expose the Order publicly or eliminate their local leadership

quests.rewards: LEVEL 6, Order becomes open enemy, anti-Order forces rally, transition to Act 3
quests.complications: Order has resources, agents, and believers everywhere. Exposing them triggers open conflict. Some people won't believe - the Order has done good things, been helpful, are trusted. This isn't a neat revelation; it's tearing society apart.
quests.secrets: Maren will flee to Felhurst when exposed. Voss will activate contingency plans - accelerating the Convergence if necessary. Some Order members like Brother Aldric will be horrified and might turn against leadership. Others will fight.
quests.notes: END OF ACT 2. Everything changes after this. The investigation is over; open conflict begins. Should feel like a point of no return.

quests.name: The Captain's Shadow
quests.description: The Order has decided Captain Edric is too dangerous - his documentation of their failures, his competence, his influence over the players. They're planning to eliminate him. Players must learn of the threat and prevent it.
quests.background: Edric has been quietly documenting anomalies for years. The Order has noticed. A plan is in motion to remove him through an 'accident' or frame-up, timed for when players are away from Tawren.

objectives.text: Learn of the threat to Edric
Identify the assassination method
Prevent the attempt
Expose the assassins' Order connections

quests.rewards: Edric survives and becomes active ally, evidence against Order, trust strengthened
quests.complications: If players fail or ignore warning signs, Edric dies mid-campaign. If careless, players might be implicated. The assassination uses a blackmailed soldier who doesn't know his true masters.
quests.secrets: Losing Edric is a major blow - he's the players' advocate, their quest-giver, their friend. His death should hurt and have consequences. If saved, he can become General and be crucial in Act 3.
quests.notes: TIME-SENSITIVE. Warning signs appear; players must act. If they're invested in Edric, this creates tension. If they fail, consequences are real.

quests.name: The Heart of Darkness
quests.description: Vaelthrix the lich cannot be permanently destroyed while his phylactery exists. It's hidden in the depths of Starfall Lake, protected by ancient wards and a guardian creature. Find it, retrieve it, destroy it.
quests.background: A lich reforms after death unless its phylactery is destroyed. Vaelthrix hid his three centuries ago in the deepest part of Starfall Lake, protected by magic and bound creature. Without destroying it, any victory at Felhurst is temporary.

objectives.text: Learn phylactery location from Aldwin's research
Travel to Starfall Lake
Find way to reach the lake depths
Defeat or bypass the guardian creature
Retrieve the phylactery
Destroy the phylactery using appropriate method

quests.rewards: Vaelthrix becomes permanently killable - victory becomes possible
quests.complications: The lake is deep and cold - requires magic, equipment, or creative solutions. The guardian is powerful and bound by old magic. Destruction requires specific methods: holy fire, a blessed weapon, or being present when the Convergence fails.
quests.secrets: Without this quest completed, killing Vaelthrix at Felhurst is only a setback - he reforms in 1d10 days. Players need to do this before the finale or be prepared for consequences.
quests.notes: IDEALLY BEFORE FINALE. Can be done in Act 3 before assaulting Felhurst. Underwater/lake adventure with different challenges.

quests.name: The Convergence
quests.description: The final battle. Storm Felhurst Ruins, fight through Order defenses and creatures from beyond, reach the ritual chamber, stop the Convergence, and confront Vaelthrix the Undying.
quests.background: Everything has led to this moment. The Order is exposed, allies are rallied (or fallen), the phylactery is destroyed (or not). The Convergence is accelerating. Time to end it.
