objectives.text: Rally available allies
Travel through Old Deadwood to Felhurst
Breach Felhurst defenses
Fight through the First Undercroft
Reach the Deep Sanctum
Stop the Convergence ritual
Defeat Vaelthrix

quests.rewards: Victory - the duchy saved. Depending on choices: Duke restored, Isara empowered, allies survived, the future secured. Or failure, with consequences.
quests.complications: Everything depends on earlier choices. Allies gathered provide support. Phylactery destruction matters for permanence. Isara's training determines her effectiveness. Every decision throughout the campaign echoes here.
quests.secrets: The ritual can be stopped by: destroying the focus crystal in the chamber, killing Vaelthrix (permanently, if phylactery destroyed), or someone with power sacrificing themselves to close the breach (Aldwin could, or Isara if she chooses). Multiple paths to victory, all costly.
quests.notes: SESSIONS 9-10. THE FINALE. Should feel like every decision mattered. Allies appear (or don't). Powers unleashed (or not). The culmination of everything.

quests.name: The Broken General
quests.description: General Harren is a drunk disgrace - but also a brilliant tactician destroyed by guilt over false intelligence at the Battle of Thornfield. Can he be redeemed?
quests.background: Harren's guilt is based on a lie - the intelligence that led him to split his forces was planted by the Order. He's not a coward; he was manipulated. The truth could break him or forge him anew.

objectives.text: Learn about Harren's past and the Battle of Thornfield
Find evidence that the intelligence was false
Decide whether to confront Harren with the truth
Help Harren through his crisis (whatever form it takes)
See Harren's redemption - or fall

quests.rewards: Redeemed Harren becomes competent General - major military asset for Act 3. Or Harren falls, requiring Edric (if alive) to take over.
quests.complications: Redemption isn't guaranteed. The truth could break him further. He might refuse to believe. He might become suicidally reckless. Player choices and roleplaying determine outcome.
quests.secrets: Evidence exists in Order records, possibly Maren's journal. The refugee Tomas from Thornfield saw Lightwardens behaving strangely that day. Multiple clues point to the truth.
quests.notes: CHARACTER ARC quest. Not completed in one session - develops over Act 2. Requires player investment. Redeemed Harren or functional replacement (Edric) is important for military capacity in Act 3.

quests.name: The Tribes Beyond
quests.description: The Osmonti tribes of the Skyless Waste are a wildcard - potential allies, potential enemies, or neutrals who might raid while Karmont is distracted. Securing their alliance (or at least neutrality) could be valuable.
quests.background: Chieftain Mordak leads the largest Osmonti band. He's pragmatic - will deal with whoever offers the best terms. The Order has been courting them. Players can counter-offer.

objectives.text: Learn about the Osmonti and their concerns
Travel to the Skyless Waste
Earn audience with Chieftain Mordak
Negotiate terms (alliance, neutrality, or specific aid)
Possibly complete a task to prove good faith

quests.rewards: Osmonti alliance provides warriors and scouts for Act 3. Neutrality at least prevents raids. Good relations open trade possibilities.
quests.complications: Osmonti culture is different - protocols matter, strength is respected, pretty words mean nothing. May require completing a trial or task. If ignored entirely, Osmonti might ally with Order or raid opportunistically.
quests.secrets: Osmonti shamans sense the wrongness from Old Deadwood - they know something terrible is building. This can be leveraged to argue common cause. Mordak secretly despises the Order missionaries.
quests.notes: DIPLOMATIC quest. Different challenge type - negotiation, cultural navigation, proving worth. Provides Act 3 military support if successful.

items.name: Ring of Gentle Repose
items.description: A simple silver band with barely visible runes on the interior. Appears to be a protective charm. Actually a curse anchor that slowly drains the wearer's mind and will.
items.properties: While worn, imposes disadvantage on Wisdom saves and Intelligence checks. Wearer loses 1 point of Intelligence and Wisdom per month (recoverable after removal). Prolonged wear causes confusion, memory loss, personality changes. Can only be identified as cursed with Identify spell or similar magic, DC 15.
items.history: Created by Order artificers, given to Duke Aldric by Steward Maren as a 'protective gift' shortly after his wife's death. Maren told him it would help him sleep and ease his grief.
items.value: Worthless as cursed item, priceless as evidence
items.notes: Removing the ring breaks the curse on the Duke. Recovery takes several days of rest and care. Ring itself is evidence of Maren's betrayal if examined by someone who knows what to look for.

items.name: Maren's Coded Journal
items.description: A leather-bound journal filled with neat handwriting in a precise, controlled hand. Appears to be administrative records and personal notes about household matters. Actually coded documentation of Maren's activities for the Order over twenty-five years.
items.properties: Written in a cipher using a book code based on the Order's holy text. DC 20 Investigation or Intelligence check to recognize as coded. DC 18 to decode with proper tools and time, or Comprehend Languages reveals it automatically. Contains: records of Duke's curse maintenance, communications with Voss, sabotage operations, references to Convergence timeline, confession of Lady Elara's murder.
items.history: Maren has kept this journal for twenty-five years as insurance, record-keeping, and perhaps a twisted form of pride in his work. Hidden in a secret compartment in his office, behind a false panel in his bookshelf.
items.value: Priceless as evidence - could bring down the Order in Karmont
items.notes: Finding and decoding this journal provides concrete proof of Order conspiracy. Key evidence for exposing them. Maren will kill to prevent its discovery.

items.name: Vaelthrix's Phylactery
items.description: A crystalline container about the size of a fist, glowing with sickly blue-green light that pulses like a heartbeat. Contains the bound soul of the lich Vaelthrix. Intensely cold to the touch, causes frost to form on nearby surfaces. Whispers in dead languages when held, the voices of souls consumed to power it.
items.properties: While intact, Vaelthrix reforms 1d10 days after being 'killed' at the phylactery's location. Can be destroyed by: holy fire (casting Sacred Flame or similar while willing destruction, DC 15 Religion check), a blessed weapon strike (requires weapon blessed by true faith, not Order), or being present when the Convergence fails (magical feedback destroys it). Attempting destruction without proper method deals 6d6 necrotic damage to the attemptee. Guardian creature (Drowned One - use Aboleth stats modified) protects it.
items.history: Created three centuries ago when Vaelthrix became a lich. Hidden in the deepest part of Starfall Lake, where the cold and pressure protect it. The guardian was bound at the same time - a creature from beyond forced to serve.
items.value: Beyond mortal currency - the key to defeating an ancient evil
items.notes: The key to permanently defeating Vaelthrix. Quest to destroy it should feel momentous. Without destruction, Felhurst victory is temporary at best.

items.name: Captain Edric's Documentation
items.description: A collection of papers, notes, and reports kept in a locked strongbox. Records of military operations over fifteen years, with annotations noting anomalies, failures, and patterns.
items.properties: Contains: lists of missions where Order 'assistance' correlated with failure, supply requisitions that were never fulfilled, intelligence reports that proved false, testimony from soldiers about strange Order behavior. Not proof by itself, but shows a pattern. Combined with other evidence, devastating.
items.history: Edric has been keeping these records for years, unable to prove anything but unwilling to ignore his instincts. Hidden in his quarters at Tawren Barracks.
items.value: 50gp to the right buyer, priceless as evidence
items.notes: Supports the case against the Order. If Edric dies, players might find this among his effects. If he lives, he'll share it when the time is right.

items.name: Charm of Vorath
items.description: A small iron hammer pendant on a leather cord, worn smooth by generations of handling. Faintly warm to the touch. The symbol of Vorath the Ironfather, now banned by the Order.
items.properties: While attuned and worn, grants +1 to AC against the first attack each combat, and advantage on saves against fear. Once per long rest, can invoke Vorath's protection to gain resistance to all damage for one round. Glows faintly warm when undead are within 60 feet.
items.history: These charms were common before the Order's ban. Most were destroyed or hidden. This one was passed down through a soldier's family in Britvold.
items.notes: Can be found or given as reward in Britvold. Represents the old faith's power. Possession could cause Order trouble for the players.

items.name: Convergence Focus Crystal
items.description: A massive crystal formation in the Deep Sanctum of Felhurst, pulsing with otherworldly energy. Colors shift through spectrums that shouldn't exist. Looking at it too long causes nausea and nosebleeds. The anchor point of the Convergence ritual.
items.properties: Cannot be moved. Destroying it (AC 18, 200 HP, immune to necrotic/poison/psychic, vulnerable to radiant) stops the Convergence but causes massive magical backlash (all creatures within 100 feet take 8d6 force damage, DC 16 Dex save for half). While the ritual runs, the crystal heals 20 HP at the start of each round unless disrupted.
items.history: Not created but grown over decades, fed by suffering and ritual magic. The crystallized form of the weakening barrier.
items.value: Cannot be valued - destroying it is the goal
items.notes: One way to stop the Convergence. Destroying it is dangerous but effective. Located in the Deep Sanctum.

shops.name: The Weary Soldier Inn
shops.description: A large, practical tavern serving Tawren's soldiers. Good ale, filling food, and rooms that are clean if not luxurious. Run by Bram Oakhollow, a former soldier who keeps order with a firm hand and a heavy club behind the bar.
shops.specialties: Soldier's Stew (hearty, 5cp), Dwarven Ale (strong, 1sp), Bram's Special (whatever's good that day, 2sp)
shops.notes: Primary tavern for Act 1. Notice board location. Bram is a good source of military gossip.

shops.name: The Golden Stag Inn
shops.description: Karmont's finest inn, catering to nobility, wealthy merchants, and important visitors. Fine rooms, excellent food, and discretion. Run by Delia Warmstone, a former minor noble with connections throughout court society.
shops.specialties: Private dining rooms, imported wines, information brokering (prices vary)
shops.notes: Upscale option in Karmont. Good for political information. Delia dislikes the Order.

shops.name: The Hunter's Rest
shops.description: A weathered tavern on Britvold's village green, serving hunters, loggers, and travelers brave enough to skirt the forest. Run by Old Marget, who's seen everything and judges everyone.
shops.specialties: Game stew (whatever was caught, 4cp), forest berry wine (local, 8cp), information about the forest (if she likes you)
shops.notes: Village tavern for forest quests. Marget has seen Order members behaving strangely.

shops.name: The Stone Ewe
shops.description: A small, cozy tavern in Innskirk, built of the same gray stone as the village houses. Serves shepherds, farmers, and the occasional traveler. The locals watch strangers carefully here.
shops.specialties: Mutton pie (filling, 6cp), hill whiskey (rough, 1sp), warmth and suspicion in equal measure
shops.notes: Key location for finding Aldwin. Must earn trust before getting information.

shops.name: Ironarm's Forge
shops.description: A well-equipped smithy run by Helga Ironarm, a dwarven smith of considerable skill and blunt opinions. Supplies the military with weapons and armor, and civilians with tools and hardware.
shops.specialties: Military equipment, weapon repairs, custom orders (with time and gold)
shops.notes: Quality equipment source. Helga has noticed Order-commissioned weapons designed to fail. Potential clue source.

shops.name: Mira's Remedies
shops.description: A cluttered shop run by Mira Softfoot, a halfling herbalist named after the goddess. Herbs hang from every rafter, potions bubble in the back, and the smell is overwhelming but not unpleasant.
shops.specialties: Healing potions, antidotes, herbal remedies, and quiet worship of the old gods
shops.notes: Potion source. Mira maintains a secret Hearthmother shrine. Has noticed Order healing sometimes making patients worse.

shops.name: Runespike Trading Post
shops.description: The surface trading post where the Runespike dwarves deal with outsiders. Quality metalwork, ore, and dwarven goods at fair prices. Run by Grenda Ironvein, Durak's sister.
shops.specialties: Dwarven weapons and armor (masterwork quality), raw ore, dwarven ale
shops.notes: Best equipment in the duchy, but remote. Dwarves are neutral in human politics but will help against supernatural threats.

maps.name: Karmont Regional Map
maps.description: The Duchy of Karmont and her outlying regions. Shows settlements (Small City, Town, Village, Settlement), roads, geographic features, and points of interest. Scale: approximately 1 inch = 10 miles.
